- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Runs `RequestPayloadStager.stage()` off the dynamic engine loop, so a slow payload write no longer pauses decoding for every active request.

Addresses [NVIDIA-NeMo/RL#4663](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/RL/issues/4663) (Megatron token capture: the TQ media write blocks the engine step).

On `main`, `_send_requests_to_coordinator` calls `payload_stager.stage()` inline for each completed request before sending replies, from the bookkeeping pass of every engine step. When the stager's write is a blocking network round trip, every finished request stalls the engine loop for the duration of its write. NeMo-RL token capture is one such stager: it writes each completed request's token delta (and, with media capture, its pixels) to a TransferQueue store.

Now each stageable completed request gets its own asyncio task:

- `_stage_and_reply` builds the `OffloadedRequestPayload` on the loop thread, runs `stage()` via `asyncio.to_thread`, then sends that request's reply from the loop thread (the ZMQ socket stays single-threaded).
- Each reply still waits for its own write, so `payload_stage_metadata` keeps describing a completed write (stage-before-ack is unchanged). Only the engine stops waiting. This matches what the NeMo-RL vLLM worker already does with the same write.
- Failed and unstaged replies are sent immediately, as before. A stager exception sends the reply unstaged instead of failing the loop.
- Tasks are held in `_staging_tasks`, because the event loop keeps only [weak references to tasks](https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#asyncio.create_task). `shutdown()` drains them before closing the socket and logs how many it waited for.
- The periodic step log reports the staging backlog (`payload staging: in-flight N, peak M`), so a write path that cannot keep up is visible.
- The `RequestPayloadStager` protocol is unchanged, and stagers need no changes.

## Results

NeMo-RL GRPO, Nemotron-3-Nano-Omni-30B-A3B on VSTAT video, token capture with media, Megatron inference, 42 steps. Overhead is the extra `exposed_generation` per step for capture on vs. off, paired per step. [W&B overlay of the generation-bound runs](https://wandb.ai/adlr/mllm-rl-dev?nw=2n1rne2a5x2).

**Generation-bound** (one TP8/EP8 generation replica, on-policy, so generation time is fully exposed):

| | capture on | capture off | extra exposed generation / step |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | [run](https://wandb.ai/adlr/mllm-rl-dev/runs/4f2asz54) | [run](https://wandb.ai/adlr/mllm-rl-dev/runs/puejmm4j) | +3.97 s (mean) / +3.82 s (median) |
| this PR | [run](https://wandb.ai/adlr/mllm-rl-dev/runs/ig3pkhci) | [run](https://wandb.ai/adlr/mllm-rl-dev/runs/gukf26yk) | +2.63 s (mean) / +2.95 s (median) |
| this PR + 6 NeMo-RL reassembler workers (instead of 2) | [run](https://wandb.ai/adlr/mllm-rl-dev/runs/98g9vssq) | [run](https://wandb.ai/adlr/mllm-rl-dev/runs/gukf26yk) | +1.54 s (mean) / +1.56 s (median) |

This PR removes the engine-side share (~1.3 s/step). The rest is on the NeMo-RL consumer side (reassembler queueing, media transfer through the store). That part is shared with the vLLM backend (same pipeline, [vLLM capture-on run](https://wandb.ai/adlr/mllm-rl-dev/runs/pjrbikqm)) and is tracked in NeMo-RL.

**Default async layout** (three generation replicas, one step of lookahead): no measurable overhead even on `main`, because generation has spare capacity and hides the write: 35.6 s vs. 36.2 s/step ([on](https://wandb.ai/adlr/mllm-rl-dev/runs/n63nmvq0), [off](https://wandb.ai/adlr/mllm-rl-dev/runs/pszdknot), [overlay](https://wandb.ai/adlr/mllm-rl-dev?nw=vd6ela6gjmk)).

## Related PRs

Megatron-LM:
- #7015: added the `RequestPayloadStager` / `RequestPromptPreparer` hooks this PR changes how the engine calls.
- #7557: hands compact prompt ids and media tensors to the payload stager (makes media writes large).
- #7598: multimodal prefix stitching used by the same capture path.

NeMo-RL:
- [NVIDIA-NeMo/RL#4332](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/RL/pull/4332): Megatron token capture with media, where this was measured. [Review comment that flagged the in-step write](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/RL/pull/4332#discussion_r4152142339), [measurements](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/RL/pull/4332#discussion_r4223398167).
- [NVIDIA-NeMo/RL#4129](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/RL/pull/4129): Megatron (MInf) token capture through the payload stager.
- [NVIDIA-NeMo/RL#4191](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/RL/pull/4191): vLLM VLM media capture; its worker already runs the same write off its engine.
- [NVIDIA-NeMo/RL#4307](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/RL/pull/4307): stages MoE routing indices through the same stager (also benefits).

## Issue tracking

Linked issue: addresses [NVIDIA-NeMo/RL#4663](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/RL/issues/4663). This PR removes the engine-side stall described there; NeMo-RL picks it up through a Megatron-Bridge bump. The rest of the overhead measured in that issue (reassembler queueing and media transfer, shared with vLLM) is NeMo-RL-side and not changed here.

- [ ] I have added relevant functional tests (verified end to end in NeMo-RL GPU runs instead; see Results)
- [ ] If this PR adds or changes a GPU kernel ... (N/A)
- [x] I have added proper typing to my code
- [ ] I have added relevant documentation (docstrings only)
- [x] I have run the autoformatter.sh on my PR (black/isort/ruff/pylint clean; mypy is advisory in the script and reports no new errors in the changed code)

**Testing notes**
- The CPU-runnable tests in `tests/unit_tests/inference/engines/test_dynamic_engine.py` were run locally: 74 passed vs. 67 on `main`, with identical pre-existing failures/errors (GPU/NCCL-only).
- `TestDynamicInferenceEngine::test_payload_offload_mode` (GPU) drives the engine with `step_modern()`, which runs the loop only during a step. It now drains the staging tasks after stepping. That change has not been run on GPU yet, so CI is its first run.

This code sits outside the `try/except`.

If there is any error raised here, it vanishes into the void. The task this is running in does get awaited with `return_exceptions=True` in `_drain_staging_tasks`, but the done callback on L1720 removes the task from `self._staging_tasks` before it can be awaited. The exception never gets raised, so for the client, a request that fails here is an infinite hang. If it happens during shutdown, there is a `return_exceptions=True`, but the exception is still dropped afterwards.

I think this can be reasonably expected to fail sometimes. I've reviewed 2 other PRs this week that have had bugs in the serialization logic, so it's a hotspot of sorts. And also, `response_metadata` is validated only at pack time, so any bug in Gym / NeMo RL can cause a silent degradation here.

So this needs a fix. Here are some options I see:

The easiest way to handle this is to decorate `_stage_and_reply` with `trace_async_exceptions`, to make the error loud, but that will cause the entire process to fail which is not ideal. Better than a silent hang still.

A good fix is to wrap the serialization and send in a `try/except` as well, and then publish any failure from this `_stage_and_reply` the same way as `_fail_submission` does, by replying to the caller with an explicit failure.

The best fix, I think, is to properly reap the exception. Instead of having a done callback that discards the task from the task list, await the task list inside the engine loop with something like:
```
if self._staging_tasks:
    done, _ = await asyncio.wait(self._staging_tasks, timeout=0)
    for task in done:
        self._staging_tasks.discard(task)
        exc = None if task.cancelled() else task.exception()
        if exc is not None:
            self._send_failed_reply(task.request, exc)
```

This waits without a timeout at shutdown.

Unfortunately, shutdown through NeMo RL will always timeout because it's not done properly; NeMo RL does not stop the engine.

So any shutdown through NeMo RL will hang here.

One option is to add a timeout here. I don't like that option, I would avoid it, but I'll leave it up to you.

Another option would be to add an issue or a comment, pointing out that NeMo RL never shuts down the engine (no `stop_engines`, no `shutdown_coordinator`, no nothing) so that a future NeMo RL PR can see the comment and handle the shutdown properly. And until that gets fixed, this hang can be at least documented this way.

Keeping the wait unbounded and adding a comment instead. I also think it's fine like this because we don't really lose more functionality in terms of token capture.

Say the engine finished requests 1–4, replies 1–3 went out, and the job died before request 4's reply was sent:

- 1–4 are separate rollouts in one prompt group: NRL keeps 1–3 if they finished and were checkpointed, and reruns 4. Gym never got 4's reply, so that rollout never finished.
- 1–4 are turns of one multi-turn rollout: the rollout never finished, so NeMo RL reruns it from turn 1, including turns 1–3.

The above is the expected behavior anyway. Only thing is that we may lose more responses than if we had a better solution, but tbh the TQ writes are quick, so it should be minimal

detail.body:
- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Runs `RequestPayloadStager.stage()` off the dynamic engine loop, so a slow payload write no longer pauses decoding for every active request.

Addresses [NVIDIA-NeMo/RL#4663](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/RL/issues/4663) (Megatron token capture: the TQ media write blocks the engine step).

On `main`, `_send_requests_to_coordinator` calls `payload_stager.stage()` inline for each completed request before sending replies, from the bookkeeping pass of every engine step. When the stager's write is a blocking network round trip, every finished request stalls the engine loop for the duration of its write. NeMo-RL token capture is one such stager: it writes each completed request's token delta (and, with media capture, its pixels) to a TransferQueue store.

Now each stageable completed request gets its own asyncio task:

- `_stage_and_reply` builds the `OffloadedRequestPayload` on the loop thread, runs `stage()` via `asyncio.to_thread`, then sends that request's reply from the loop thread (the ZMQ socket stays single-threaded).
- Each reply still waits for its own write, so `payload_stage_metadata` keeps describing a completed write (stage-before-ack is unchanged). Only the engine stops waiting. This matches what the NeMo-RL vLLM worker already does with the same write.
- Failed and unstaged replies are sent immediately, as before. A stager exception sends the reply unstaged instead of failing the loop.
- Tasks are held in `_staging_tasks`, because the event loop keeps only [weak references to tasks](https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#asyncio.create_task). `shutdown()` drains them before closing the socket and logs how many it waited for.
- The periodic step log reports the staging backlog (`payload staging: in-flight N, peak M`), so a write path that cannot keep up is visible.
- The `RequestPayloadStager` protocol is unchanged, and stagers need no changes.

## Results

NeMo-RL GRPO, Nemotron-3-Nano-Omni-30B-A3B on VSTAT video, token capture with media, Megatron inference, 42 steps. Overhead is the extra `exposed_generation` per step for capture on vs. off, paired per step. [W&B overlay of the generation-bound runs](https://wandb.ai/adlr/mllm-rl-dev?nw=2n1rne2a5x2).

**Generation-bound** (one TP8/EP8 generation replica, on-policy, so generation time is fully exposed):

| | capture on | capture off | extra exposed generation / step |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | [run](https://wandb.ai/adlr/mllm-rl-dev/runs/4f2asz54) | [run](https://wandb.ai/adlr/mllm-rl-dev/runs/puejmm4j) | +3.97 s (mean) / +3.82 s (median) |
| this PR | [run](https://wandb.ai/adlr/mllm-rl-dev/runs/ig3pkhci) | [run](https://wandb.ai/adlr/mllm-rl-dev/runs/gukf26yk) | +2.63 s (mean) / +2.95 s (median) |
| this PR + 6 NeMo-RL reassembler workers (instead of 2) | [run](https://wandb.ai/adlr/mllm-rl-dev/runs/98g9vssq) | [run](https://wandb.ai/adlr/mllm-rl-dev/runs/gukf26yk) | +1.54 s (mean) / +1.56 s (median) |

This PR removes the engine-side share (~1.3 s/step). The rest is on the NeMo-RL consumer side (reassembler queueing, media transfer through the store). That part is shared with the vLLM backend (same pipeline, [vLLM capture-on run](https://wandb.ai/adlr/mllm-rl-dev/runs/pjrbikqm)) and is tracked in NeMo-RL.

**Default async layout** (three generation replicas, one step of lookahead): no measurable overhead even on `main`, because generation has spare capacity and hides the write: 35.6 s vs. 36.2 s/step ([on](https://wandb.ai/adlr/mllm-rl-dev/runs/n63nmvq0), [off](https://wandb.ai/adlr/mllm-rl-dev/runs/pszdknot), [overlay](https://wandb.ai/adlr/mllm-rl-dev?nw=vd6ela6gjmk)).

## Related PRs

Megatron-LM:
- #7015: added the `RequestPayloadStager` / `RequestPromptPreparer` hooks this PR changes how the engine calls.
- #7557: hands compact prompt ids and media tensors to the payload stager (makes media writes large).
- #7598: multimodal prefix stitching used by the same capture path.

NeMo-RL:
- [NVIDIA-NeMo/RL#4332](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/RL/pull/4332): Megatron token capture with media, where this was measured. [Review comment that flagged the in-step write](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/RL/pull/4332#discussion_r4152142339), [measurements](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/RL/pull/4332#discussion_r4223398167).
- [NVIDIA-NeMo/RL#4129](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/RL/pull/4129): Megatron (MInf) token capture through the payload stager.
- [NVIDIA-NeMo/RL#4191](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/RL/pull/4191): vLLM VLM media capture; its worker already runs the same write off its engine.
- [NVIDIA-NeMo/RL#4307](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/RL/pull/4307): stages MoE routing indices through the same stager (also benefits).

## Issue tracking

Linked issue: addresses [NVIDIA-NeMo/RL#4663](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/RL/issues/4663). This PR removes the engine-side stall described there; NeMo-RL picks it up through a Megatron-Bridge bump. The rest of the overhead measured in that issue (reassembler queueing and media transfer, shared with vLLM) is NeMo-RL-side and not changed here.

- [x] I have added relevant unit tests (`test_slow_stager_does_not_block_the_engine_loop`, `test_stager_error_keeps_payload_on_the_reply`, `test_drain_waits_for_in_flight_staging`, `test_staging_backlog_is_reported_in_the_step_log`, `test_staging_backlog_log_is_empty_without_a_stager`, `test_drain_logs_the_in_flight_count`, `test_drain_is_silent_when_nothing_is_in_flight`; the existing offload/ledger reply tests now run in an event loop)
- [ ] I have added relevant functional tests (verified end to end in NeMo-RL GPU runs instead; see Results)
- [ ] If this PR adds or changes a GPU kernel ... (N/A)
- [x] I have added proper typing to my code
- [ ] I have added relevant documentation (docstrings only)
- [x] I have run the autoformatter.sh on my PR (black/isort/ruff/pylint clean; mypy is advisory in the script and reports no new errors in the changed code)

**Testing notes**
- The CPU-runnable tests in `tests/unit_tests/inference/engines/test_dynamic_engine.py` were run locally: 74 passed vs. 67 on `main`, with identical pre-existing failures/errors (GPU/NCCL-only).
- `TestDynamicInferenceEngine::test_payload_offload_mode` (GPU) drives the engine with `step_modern()`, which runs the loop only during a step. It now drains the staging tasks after stepping. That change has not been run on GPU yet, so CI is its first run.

This code sits outside the `try/except`.

If there is any error raised here, it vanishes into the void. The task this is running in does get awaited with `return_exceptions=True` in `_drain_staging_tasks`, but the done callback on L1720 removes the task from `self._staging_tasks` before it can be awaited. The exception never gets raised, so for the client, a request that fails here is an infinite hang. If it happens during shutdown, there is a `return_exceptions=True`, but the exception is still dropped afterwards.

I think this can be reasonably expected to fail sometimes. I've reviewed 2 other PRs this week that have had bugs in the serialization logic, so it's a hotspot of sorts. And also, `response_metadata` is validated only at pack time, so any bug in Gym / NeMo RL can cause a silent degradation here.

So this needs a fix. Here are some options I see:

The easiest way to handle this is to decorate `_stage_and_reply` with `trace_async_exceptions`, to make the error loud, but that will cause the entire process to fail which is not ideal. Better than a silent hang still.

A good fix is to wrap the serialization and send in a `try/except` as well, and then publish any failure from this `_stage_and_reply` the same way as `_fail_submission` does, by replying to the caller with an explicit failure.

The best fix, I think, is to properly reap the exception. Instead of having a done callback that discards the task from the task list, await the task list inside the engine loop with something like:
```
if self._staging_tasks:
    done, _ = await asyncio.wait(self._staging_tasks, timeout=0)
    for task in done:
        self._staging_tasks.discard(task)
        exc = None if task.cancelled() else task.exception()
        if exc is not None:
            self._send_failed_reply(task.request, exc)
```
